title: Infinite Fourier Tails and High-Mode Coercivity for the Semilocal Weil Quadratic Form
description:
Connes, Consani and Moscovici encode the semilocal Weil quadratic form on [C-1/2, C1/2] by an infinite real symmetric matrix A(C) in a Fourier basis. This preprint proves three rank-independent estimates for how that infinite matrix acts on a truncated ground state: an exact signed-moment identity for the omitted components of A c with a remainder uniform over infinitely many indices; the operator bound ||Aoff|| ≤ 2π supi |bi| via the discrete Hilbert transform; and explicit logarithmic coercivity of high-mode compressions.

Combined with validated interval enclosures of the rank-eight even ground vector u(C), the result holds uniformly over the cell 17 ≤ C ≤ 19: the even components of A(C) u(C) at every Fourier index j > 64 have joint ℓ2 norm below 9.491 × 10-12, and the even and full compressions of A(C) to sufficiently high modes exceed the identity. Infinite-index statements are proved analytically; finite-dimensional quantities are certified by outward-rounded ball arithmetic (Arb via python-flint) and replayed by an independent mpmath implementation.

The estimates do not bound the intermediate modes, give no uniform budget over all ranks and supports, and do not identify any limit with Riemann's Ξ function. The Riemann Hypothesis is not claimed. The attached archive contains the certificate generators, the regression suite and the replay scripts.
